To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the ichnogenus Scalihnus is a potential taphonomic implement to understand multi-storm events in the sedimentary record; and (ii) the ichnogenera Scalichnus can be used to sequence a series of amalgamate storm events in a sedimentary sequence, to assess the magnitude and frequency, and to analyse the positive taphonomy effect of these equilibrium burrows.
Scalichnus trace fossils can be used as sedimentological tools to assess storm frequency, intensity and magnitude, as well as to infer the background taphonomic processes.
The fossil record is characterized by time- averaged assemblages as consequence of the mixture in a single horizon of multiple generations of fossils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of sequestering information inside burrows, and the use of these trace fossils as a tool to investigate taphonomic processes.
the study of the taphonomic effects of storm events and their consequences for the preservation of the fossil record.
the potential of sequestered taphonomic information inside trace fossils to reconstruct past events.

the taphonomic analysis carried out on the studied fossil assemblages provides evidence that a multi-storm event occurred in the area during deposition.
the ichnofabric of Scalichnus is a potential proxy of multi-storm events, and therefore a useful tool in sedimentological studies.

the taphonomic analysis carried out on Scalichnus is a good example of how the study of trace fossils can provide information about the sedimentological processes and the environmental conditions of the time of formation.
